caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1470 of 2004
lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, with Probir Neogi, Advocate, instructed by Md. Ahsan Ullah Patwary, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner. 
Respondents ----- Not represented.
parties:
Sree Girish Chandra Barman ----- Petitioner.

Md. Yasin Ali and other ----- Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16th May, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3948 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J : This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 16.5.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3948 of 2002 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and order dated 18.5.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Lalmonirhat in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 6 of 1999 affirming, with some modification, those of dated 30.11.1998 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Lalmonirhat Sadar, in Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1996 refusing pre-emption.

2. The petitioner, the pre-emptor, filed the above Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1996 for pre-emption of the case land under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 stating, inter alia, that he is a co-sharer in the case holding by inheritance; his brother, the respondent No. 2, by a sale deed dated 17.06.95 transferred the case land to the pre-emptee, the respondent No.1, a stranger to the case holding; on notice about the above sale dated 17.6.95 not being served upon the pre-emptor he was totally ignorant of the transfer till 27.10.96; the respondent No. 2 by sale deed dated 22.6.1996 having sold some other land of the case holding to the above pre-emptee he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1996 wherein the pre-emptee, on 27.10.1996, filed written objection disclosing therein the earlier transfer to him by sale deed dated 17.06.95 and then only he, for the first time, came to know about the above sale deed dated 17.06.95; he then after obtaining the certified copy. of the said deed filed the case seeking pre-emption, although in the above sale deed dated 17.6.95 the khatian number has been shown as 160, actually it would be Khatian No. 13. The pre-emptee-respondent no.1 contested the pre-emption case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that he purchased the case land from the respondent No.2 for construction of his residence and he went into possession of the case land on 18.06.95 and he then raised dwelling house thereon at the cost of Tk.25,000/- and that the pre-emptor is no longer a co-sharer in the case holding.

<u>3. The trial court, after hearing, refused pre-emption holding that the pre-emptor ceased to be a co-sharer of the case holding due to splitting up of jama and the case is also barred by limitation. The pre-emptor preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.6 of 1999 which was also dismissed. The pre-emptor then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 4197 of 2000. The pre-emptor earlier also obtained another Rule in Civil Revision No. 4196 of 2000 which was preferred against judgment and order dated 3.11.1998 Passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5 of 1999 affirming the judgment and order dated 30.11.98 in Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1996 refusing pre-emption in respect of sale deed dated 22.6.1996. The above Rules were heard analogously and the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 19.08.2001 made the Rules absolute remanding the appeals to the lower appellate court. On receiving the records the lower appellate court, dismissed the appeal holding as follows:</u>

<u>"In the light of discussion made above I may conclude that the alleged R.S. Khatian No. 160 was finally published on 6.05.98 i.e. long after the transfer of the case land to O.P. No. 1 i.e. at the time of transfer of even at the time of entry in volume of the case land is in law a part of S.A. plot No. 40 of S.A. Khatian No. 13. In law it cannot be said that the case land was a part of R.S. plot No. 88 or R.S. Khatian No. 160, and it was splitted up from the S.A. Khatian No. 13. So I can conclude at the time of transfer of the case land the petitioner appellant was a co-sharer by dint of holding. According to section 2(13) "Holding" means parcel or parcels of land or an undivided share thereof held by reiyat or an under rayat from the subject of separate tenancy.</u>

<u>Moreover in perusing the S.A. map adduced by the appellant it is seen that S.A. plot No. 40 is a compact plot. The further contention of the appellant is that he is a co-sharer by purchase in the case jama by purchasing 23 decimals of land plot No. 40 of khatian No. 13. The appellant has produced the original kabala dated 2.1.88 to substantiate his contention (Ext.3). In the light of discussion made above I may conclude that the appellant is co-sharer in the case jama by dint of holding and purchase as well by the kabala dated 2.01.88 and accordingly does not need to seek pre-emption of the case land as adjoining land owner. So the trial court is not at all justified in holding the view that the case is bad for defect of parties for not impleading the adjoining land owners. The record transpires that the petitioner appellant has impleaded all S.A. recorded tenants (including Aszar Ali). So I can concluded that the instant case is not bad for defect of parties. It is categorically admitted that the O.P respondent No.1 is a stranger in the case Jama."</u>

4. On the point of limitation the lower appellate court concurred with the decision of the trial court holding that:

"the trial court made an elaborate discussion on this point and rightly concluded that the Misc Pre-emption case is hopelessly barred by limitation."

5. On revision, the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule holding that the trial court as well as the lower appellate court considered all the evidence in details and recorded a clear finding that the pre-emptor could not prove that the pre-emption proceeding was filed within four months from the date of his alleged knowledge and thus the pre-emption proceeding is barred by limitation.

6. The Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division was wrong in discharging the Rule inasmuch as the decisions of the trial court and lower appellate court on the point of limitation were founded on record; having regard to the credibility of P.Ws. compared to that of O.P.Ws pre-ponderence of evidence does not lead to the conclusion that the pre-emption case was barred by limitation; the trial court has not even mentioned the most consistent corroborative and credible evidence of the P.Ws. far less to speak of considering the same and that the decisions of the trial court as well as the lower appellate court are based on total misreading and non-consideration of evidence adduced by the pre-emptor.

<u>7. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that admittedly the transfer was made by the sale deed executed on 17.06.95 and registered under section 60 of the Registration Act on 31.07.95 and the pre-emption proceeding was filed on 31.10.96 and so the pre-emption case was not filed within four months from the date of the registration of the sale deed; the pre-emptor alleged that he learnt about the transfer in question for the first item on 27.10.96 when the opposite party no. 1 and 2 filed their written objection in Pre-emption Case No. 46 of 1996 but the pre-emptor did not examine himself before the court to prove the same and instead got his son examined as P.W.1 though it is not the case of the pre-emptor that his son came to know about the transfer in question for the first time on 27.10.96 from the contents of the 1996; the other two witnesses examined by the pre-emptor did not say anything about the knowledge of the pre-emotor about the kabala in question as alleged in the application for pre-emption; the lower appellate court noticed that P.W. No.2, one of the brother of the pre-emptor, stated that possession of the case land was delivered to the pre-emptee on the next day of the transfer that is on 18.06.95 and the further stated that the pre-emptor knew about the sale of the case land from the very beginning; the trial court as well as the lower appellate court considered all the evidence in details and concurrently found the preemptor could not prove that the preemption proceeding was filed written four months from the date of his alleged knowledge and the above finding cannot be disturbed by the High Court Division unless there is misreading/non reading of evidence or non consideration of evidence and the materials on record but the learned advocate for the petitioner could not point out any such misreading/non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of evidence/ materials on record.</u>

8. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of materials on record arrived at a correct decision and there is no cogent reason to interfere with the decision of the High Court Division.

9. The petition is dismissed.

End.
